messages.subject: using xlim in plot.scanone()
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

This might be super obvious but I can't figure out how to use the xlim
function in plot.scanone(). I want to show the lod graph between 50
and 100 cm only for a single chromosome.

Any help would be appreciated

-T

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] using xlim in plot.scanone()
messages.body_plain:
It should work to just include it in the call.  Consider the following.
You might want to use xaxs="i" (see the help file for the par function).

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)
plot(out, chr=1, xlim=c(20,60))
plot(out, chr=1, xlim=c(20,60), xaxs="i")

cheers,
karl

messages.subject: 2 part model
messages.body_plain:
I have small data set (n=100) with a large spike of unaffected mice
and then a normal distribution of affected ones.  The 2 part model
seems the most appropriate model for this data.  When I map the data
with this model I get several suggestive qtl after permutation testing
(1000x).  This model really tests 4 models simultaneously.  In several
instances the overall model is suggestive but the lod.p model is
significant.

Is it appropriate to report the individual results of the lod.p.mu <http://lod.p.mu>,
lod.p, lod.mu <http://lod.mu>?  Is it possible to graph each of the output of this
model by chromosome or genome wide?  If so is it possible to add the
individual thresholds (from permutation testing) for each of the
parameters (lod.p.mu <http://lod.p.mu>, lod.p, lod.mu <http://lod.mu>) to the graph?

Basically, I'd like to show a graph like fig2 of Boyartchuk etal and
I'm having some trouble.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] 2 part model
messages.body_plain:
Here is some example code:

   data(listeria)
   listeria <- calc.genoprob(listeria, step=1)
   listeria$pheno$T264 <- log2(listeria$pheno$T264)

   out <- scanone(listeria, model="2part", upper=TRUE)
   operm <- scanone(listeria, model="2part", upper=TRUE, n.perm=100)
   thr <- summary(operm, 0.05)

   plot(out, lod=1:3, chr=c(1,5,13,15))
   abline(h=thr, col=c("black","blue","red"), lty=2)

   text(0, thr[1]+0.1, expression(LOD(p,mu)), adj=c(0,0.5))
   text(0, thr[2]-0.1, expression(LOD(p)), adj=c(0,0.5), col="blue")
   text(0, thr[3]+0.1, expression(LOD(mu)), adj=c(0,0.5), col="red")

karl

just recognize the single largest LOD score peak on each chromosome.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] summary.scanone
messages.body_plain:
As stated in the help file (http://www.rqtl.org/manual/html/summary.scanone.html
), summary.scanone gives just the single largest LOD score on each
chromosome.

There is no easy way to pull out multiple peaks on a chromosome, and
with a single-QTL genome scan, one cannot reliably infer the presence
of multiple QTL on a chromosome from the shape of the LOD curve.  It
is best to use scantwo (to study the possibility of two linked QTL on
a chromosome) or some of the multiple-QTL model analyses, such as
fitqtl, addqtl, and addpair.

karl
